title: What to Watch This Week: A Hirani OTT Debut, Ryan Gosling in Space, and Netflix's First Telugu Original
excerpt: From a grandmother who wants to remarry to a sex-ed officer in a village with too many babies — your 4th of July streaming guide has never looked this stacked.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • This week features seven diverse streaming releases across Bollywood, Hollywood, and Telugu cinema.
  • Rajkumar Hirani's *Pritam and Pedro* debuts on JioHotstar with a cybercrime thriller theme.
  • Ryan Gosling stars in *Project Hail Mary*, a sci-fi film streaming on Amazon Prime Video.
  • Netflix's *Dadi Ki Shaadi* explores family dynamics with a grandmother wanting to remarry.
  • Telugu original *Super Subbu* tackles sex education in a comedic village setting on Netflix.
Streaming Highlights This Week
›Seven new releases across various platforms.
›Genres include cybercrime, sci-fi, family drama, and comedy.
›Notable stars include Ryan Gosling, Arshad Warsi, and Neetu Kapoor.
›Available on platforms like Netflix, Amazon Prime, and JioHotstar.
The streaming gods have conspired to give you one of the most loaded weeks of the year. Whether you're nursing a Fourth of July hangover stateside, curled up in London rain, or doom-scrolling from Toronto at 2 AM, here are seven new releases — spanning Bollywood, Hollywood, Telugu, and beyond — that genuinely deserve your time this weekend. ## 1. Pritam and Pedro — JioHotstar, July 3 *The pick if you grew up on Munna Bhai.* https://youtube.com/watch?v=m08TxIsFTRI **Rajkumar Hirani** has finally entered the OTT arena — as a producer, yes, but the fingerprints are unmistakable. Directed by **Avinash Arun**, *Pritam and Pedro* pairs **Arshad Warsi** with Hirani's own son **Vir Hirani** in a Goa-set cybercrime thriller that's getting early comparisons to Hirani's signature blend of heart and humor. **Vikrant Massey**, **Boman Irani**, and **Mona Singh** round out a cast that reads like a greatest-hits reunion. The premise — a reformed hacker and an old-school cop forced to team up on a high-profile kidnapping — is classic odd-couple territory, but with this pedigree, it could be special. Streaming on JioHotstar; available internationally through the JioHotstar app. ## 2. Project Hail Mary — Amazon Prime Video, July 3 *The pick if you like your existential crises with a side of astrophysics.* **Ryan Gosling** wakes up alone on a spaceship. No memory. No crew. Just the slow, terrifying realization that humanity's survival depends entirely on him. Based on **Andy Weir's** bestselling novel — the same mind behind *The Martian* — and directed by the *Spider-Verse* duo **Phil Lord and Christopher Miller**, this is blockbuster sci-fi landing day-and-date on streaming, which almost never happens. **Sandra Hüller** co-stars. If you loved *Interstellar* or *Arrival*, clear your evening. Streaming globally on Prime Video. ![Fourth of July — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/6/68/Fourth_of_July_fireworks_behind_the_Washington_Monument%2C_1986.jpg) > **"Reviews are mixed — 70% on Rotten Tomatoes, the weakest score of the franchise — but "weakest Enola" is still a perfectly enjoyable two hours."** ## 3. Dadi Ki Shaadi — Netflix, July 3 *The pick if your WhatsApp family group needs a conversation starter.* **Neetu Kapoor** plays a grandmother who drops a bombshell: she wants to remarry. Cue the family meltdown. Directed by **Ashwiny Iyer Tiwari** (*Bareilly Ki Barfi*), the film co-stars **Kapil Sharma** as comic relief and — in a genuine novelty — **Riddhima Kapoor Sahni** making her acting debut alongside her mother. The setup is pure desi family chaos: a progressive matriarch versus her traditionalist children, generational values colliding over something as radical as love after loss. It's warm, it's messy, and it will spark a debate at every NRI dinner table this weekend. On Netflix worldwide. https://www.instagram.com/reel/DaUX7AMiM1p/ ## 4. Super Subbu — Netflix, July 2 *The pick if you appreciate the South doing what Bollywood won't.* Netflix's **first-ever Telugu original** has arrived, and it swings hard. **Sundeep Kishan** plays Subbu, a well-meaning city guy posted as a sex education officer in Maakipur — a village where the average household has three children and absolutely nobody talks about why. With **Mithila Palkar** and the legendary **Brahmanandam** in the cast, *Super Subbu* tackles taboo with comedy and more originality in its premise than half of what Bollywood released this quarter. If you've been sleeping on Telugu content, this is your alarm clock. On Netflix with Hindi dubs. ## 5. Enola Holmes 3 — Netflix, July 1 *The pick for a breezy afternoon watch.*

![Munna Bhai — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/1/1d/Munna_Bhai.jpg) The trilogy wraps with **Millie Bobby Brown** taking her Victorian detective to Malta for a wedding-turned-kidnapping caper. **Henry Cavill** returns as Sherlock, and Moriarty makes a comeback as the big villain. Reviews are mixed — 70% on Rotten Tomatoes, the weakest score of the franchise — but "weakest Enola" is still a perfectly enjoyable two hours. Think comfort food with a feminist edge: charming enough to justify the couch, just not sharp enough to justify the hype. Available on Netflix in English, Hindi, Tamil, and Telugu. ## 6. Silo Season 3 — Apple TV+, July 3 *The pick if you like your dystopia slow-burn and devastating.* The critically adored sci-fi series based on **Hugh Howey's** novels returns with **Rebecca Ferguson** at the helm of one of the most underseen prestige shows on any platform. If you haven't started *Silo*, consider this your intervention — it's a tense underground thriller about secrets, survival, and the lies civilizations tell themselves. Season 2 ended on a cliffhanger that had Reddit in meltdown. On Apple TV+, available globally. ## 7. Isakapatnam — Amazon Prime Video, July 2 *The pick if you want your revenge cold, coastal, and 1990s.* A seven-episode Telugu thriller set in a fictional port town ruled by one man everyone wants dead. **Samuthirakani** and **Aishwarya Rajesh** lead a layered ensemble in a story about overlapping conspiracies, simmering grudges, and the messy mathematics of justice in a place where the law doesn't reach. It's atmospheric, it's gritty, and it's exactly the kind of mid-budget regional crime drama that India does better than almost anyone. On Prime Video in Telugu, Tamil, and Hindi. --- **The Verdict:** Start with *Pritam and Pedro* for the Indian pick. Start with *Project Hail Mary* for the spectacle. Save *Super Subbu* for when you want to be surprised. And text your mom about *Dadi Ki Shaadi* — trust me, she'll have opinions.
